D013-D008_h001.question:
It’s been about five months now where I’ve just felt…flat, maybe worse than flat. Most days I wake up already feeling like there’s a weight on my chest, like I’m just down in a hole I can’t climb out of. My wife will ask how I’m doing and I kind of stare at her for a bit before I answer; even talking feels slowed down, like my brain and mouth are moving through mud.

At work on the roofs, I keep thinking I’m useless, like they could grab any guy off the street and he’d do a better job. I used to be proud of what I do, but now I just feel like a burden to my crew and my family. I catch myself thinking they’d all be better off without me.

I’ve thought about ending it. I’ve pictured going out to one of the remote sites alone, waiting until everyone’s gone, and using my safety rope to hang myself where I wouldn’t be found right away. I don’t really get those “up” times people talk about—no periods where I’m super energetic or not sleeping for days or doing wild stuff. Even when I’m a little less down for a day or two, it never flips into feeling overly good or wired; it’s just more of the same heaviness.
D013-D008_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D013-D008_h002.question:

My boss has hinted about “performance concerns,” which just makes me feel worse.

I’m constantly on edge physically. I can’t sit still in my chair—I’m jiggling my leg, rubbing my hands together, getting up to pace the hallway for no real reason. At home my husband tells me to “just relax,” but I can’t.

I beat myself up over everything: if I misplace a file, I’ll dwell on it for hours, telling myself I’m a terrible employee and a burden to my team and my family. I keep thinking my husband and kids would be better off without me. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself wishing I wouldn’t wake up.

Sometimes I’ll have brief bursts where I feel a little more energized or irritable and stay up late cleaning or reorganizing things, but it never lasts more than a day or so, and I’ve never had those long, high-energy, no-sleep stretches people describe.
D013-D008_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D013-D008_h003.question:

I’ve also started having these intense waves of guilt that don’t even make sense. I catch a news story about an accident or layoffs somewhere, and I get this conviction that it’s somehow my fault, like me being a bad person caused it.

Sometimes, when I’m crossing the street or standing on the edge of the train platform, I get this sudden urge to step out, to just end it. I haven’t made any plans, but the impulse feels scarily strong.

I’ve never had a time where I felt over-energized or “on top of the world” or needed less sleep or anything like that—no high phases, just this long, dragging low that’s messing with my job and my life.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder

    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
